title: EPIC: unify retry/backoff across all 9 language targets (shared spec)
description: UR found the retry algorithm is hand-rolled separately in each target and has drifted on every axis: 4 different base delays (0.5 vs 1.0s), 4 jitter formulas, 3 retry counts (3/5/default), inconsistent Retry-After capping/parsing. Same 503 -> different load profile per client. Architectural fix: a single shared retry spec (constants + delay formula + Retry-After handling) emitted from one template, like ENCODE_URL_COMPONENT was unified. Children cover the specific correctness items. Found in UR of test-coverage-expansion.

Commits: myairtable 8530a5f, myairtable-tests b290929. All in-toolchain suites pass.

title: Retry: do not retry non-idempotent writes (POST create / no-merge upsert) on 5xx/timeout
description: H1. create (POST) and performUpsert-without-merge-fields retry on 5xx + read-timeout in Rust, TS/JS, and Python. A 5xx/timeout AFTER the server applied the write duplicates it on retry. Airtable has NO idempotency keys, so retry is the only defense and duplicate rows corrupt rollups/double-fire automations. Python worst: urllib3 allowed_methods=None fully disables the method whitelist -> POST/PATCH retried. Policy: idempotent ops (GET/list, PATCH-by-id, DELETE-by-id, merge-upsert WITH fieldsToMergeOn) retry 429+5xx+timeout; non-idempotent (plain create, upsert w/o merge) retry 429-only + connect-before-send, never 5xx-after-send/read-timeout. Rust: split is_timeout (dangerous) from is_connect (safe). Found in UR.
close_reason: Implemented unified retry/backoff across all 9 targets: idempotency policy (create/no-merge-upsert not retried on 5xx/timeout), 30s cap on backoff+Retry-After, jitter added to Swift/Kotlin + full jitter in Rust, RFC-9110 HTTP-date Retry-After parsing everywhere, Rust RateLimited carries retry_after, Python urllib3 excludes POST. Commits: myairtable 8530a5f, myairtable-tests b290929. All in-toolchain suites pass.

title: TS/JS filter DSL: FIND-based ops (contains/startsWith/...) don't escape quotes/backslashes
description:
Found by TC2 (myairtable-4ecx). In static/typescript/formula.ts and static/javascript/formula.js, wrapValue() interpolated user values into a double-quoted formula literal with NO escaping, so contains()/startsWith()/endsWith()/notContains() (all routed through FIND->wrapValue) produced malformed formulas for values containing a double quote (Airtable 422 INVALID_FILTER_BY_FORMULA). equals()/notEquals() escaped quotes but not backslashes. Other 7 targets (incl. C# reference) escape correctly.

Fix: added escapeFormulaString() (backslash-first, then quote, matching C# EscapeFormulaString) used by wrapValue; equals/notEquals now use it too (also escapes backslashes; trim/lower branches pass raw value through wrapValue to avoid double-escaping). Added TS+JS unit regressions (319 unit tests pass) and live escaping integration tests pass on all 9 targets.

title: Java language support (v2 plan)
description:
Epic: Add Java as the seventh language target for myairtable code generation.

Reference: .beads/java-plan-v2.md (user-approved 2026-06-12).

Goals:
- Full-parity generator in src/generators/java.py + static/java/
- Idiomatic Java 21: POJOs+Builders, sealed interfaces+records, unchecked exceptions, blocking API
- Integration tests in myairtable-tests/java/ at parity with Kotlin/Swift/Rust/TS/JS/Python
- CLI + checks.sh/test.sh/build.sh wiring in both repos

Key locked decisions (user-approved 2026-06-12):
- Java 21 LTS; Gradle; JDK java.net.http.HttpClient + Jackson databind; synchronous blocking API
- Models: public no-arg ctor (Jackson creator), @JsonProperty=field IDs, field-access mode, getters/setters (computed=no setter), generated Builder = creation idiom, snapshot dirty tracking, hand-rolled writable-only payloads
- JsonNode as type-erased value; ALL coercions (V/N/S/A/AN/AS/D/isTruthy) static on AirtableRuntime
- VecOrValue/MaybeSpecialOrError: sealed interface + nested records; ContextualDeserializer registered AT THE FIELD by generator
- Filter DSL eq/neq; flat package myairtable; no build-file emission; _java_ident underscore-suffix keyword rename
- Duration wire = numeric seconds (NO jackson-datatype-jsr310); Instant 3-format parser; EXP(1.0) pin
- Per-model fluent save()/fetch()/delete() via static ModelOps (no reified generics in Java)

Exit criteria:
- uv run main.py java <folder> generates compiling Java source set
- All 10 integration test files green; checks.sh + test.sh all green in both repos (7 languages)
- 16 java_static unit test files (Kotlin parity); formula builder + runtime counts within ±5% of Rust/Kotlin

title: Transpiled '{numField} = 5' is constant-false in Kotlin (JsonPrimitive 5.0 vs 5 content mismatch); audit Swift
description: Empirically proven: kotlin emitter produces JsonPrimitive(N(V(this.x))) == JsonPrimitive(5); N() returns Double so content '5.0' != '5' — every integer-literal (in)equality in runtime-evaluated formulas is wrong ({qty} = 0, {status} != 1...). Decimal literals accidentally work; < > <= >= unaffected; SWITCH immune (S() collapses). test_formula_transpiler_kotlin.py test_numeric_equality enshrines the bug. Fix in _emit_eq_operand/NumberLiteral kotlin eq-path: emit Double-form literal (JsonPrimitive(5.0)) or route =/!= through an EQ(a,b) runtime helper with S/N coercion like SWITCH. Swift is structurally identical (.double(N(...)) == .int(5)) — audit + fix there too.
close_reason: Kotlin =/!= now route through N()/S() coercion when either side's type is inferable (also fixes field-vs-numeric-expression equality); raw JsonElement equality only for uninferable pairs (parity). Dead kotlin _emit_eq_operand branch removed. 43 transpiler tests + 3 new evaluation-shape regression tests green; regenerated output; live TestRuntimeFormulas matches API. Swift/Rust share the structural bug — filing follow-up.

title: Formula.kt string escaping incomplete — filter injection via backslash/quote (Kotlin + Swift)
description: wrapValueStr escapes double-quote but NOT backslash: a value ending in backslash leaves the closing quote live and the remainder is interpreted as formula code (filter rewriting, e.g. OR(TRUE()) exfiltrates a table). Zero escaping in: FormulaId.eq (RECORD_ID()='$id' — single-quote breakout), FormulaDateLiteral DATETIME_PARSE('$value'), phoneEquals normalized value, regexMatch (quote-only). Fix: shared escapeFormulaString (backslash FIRST, then quote) + single-quote-context escaping or recXXX validation for ids. static/swift/Formula.swift:56 has the same gap.
close_reason: Both targets hardened: escapeFormulaString (backslash-first, then quote) + escapeFormulaStringSingle routed through wrapValueStr, phoneEquals, regexMatch, FormulaId eq/equals, date literals in Kotlin Formula.kt AND Swift Formula.swift. Benign values produce identical output (all 92+86 existing formula tests untouched); regex \d round-trips via Airtable string unescaping. 6 Kotlin + 5 Swift injection regression tests green.

title: Spike: does internal schema carry resolved resultType for computed fields?
description:
The pivotal unknown. Against the live base:
1. Fetch internal application/read schema (already done by _read_application_data). For computed fields (formula, multipleLookupValues, rollup, count), inspect columns[].type + typeOptions — is there a resolved resultType (and what shape: nested type object? a type string? does it cover lookups/rollups/count, not just formula?).
2. Coverage: cross-reference with find_type_ambiguities (the public-API ambiguous population). For how many of those does the internal schema give a concrete result type? Quantify.
3. Capture getUnsavedColumnConfigResultType (POST table/{tblId}/getUnsavedColumnConfigResultType) response shape for an existing formula field (the formula-only fallback): {pass, resultType}? resultType shape?
4. Compare a sample of internal resolved types vs our current field.result_type() inference — where do they diverge (these are the wins)?
Deliverable: findings appended to docs/airtable-internal-api.md; go/no-go on schema-first + whether validator fallback is needed.
notes:
SPIKE COMPLETE — GO on schema-first (docs/airtable-internal-api.md 'Investigation 2026-06-10 — computed-field type resolution').
- typeOptions.resultType present for formula/rollup/count/lookup. Coverage: 1169/1187 (98%) of all computed; 389/389 (100%) of the public-ambiguous population.
- Lookups are internal type 'lookup' (NOT multipleLookupValues) — resolver must key on internal type. They carry resultType+resultIsArray+foreignTableRollupColumnType+format.
- resultType vocab: text/number/date/checkbox + resultIsArray. Refinements in typeOptions recover finer types (isDateTime/dateFormat/timeFormat for date-vs-dateTime; format/precision/symbol for currency/percent) -> no regression vs our inference.
- Validator fallback getUnsavedColumnConfigResultType is a POST (404 on GET) -> needs deferred write transport (CSRF+secretSocketId). NOT needed for v1 given 98%/100% schema coverage. Defer.
Resolver should normalize typeOptions.{resultType,resultIsArray,isDateTime,format} -> codegen type vocabulary.
close_reason: Spike complete: GO on schema-first. Internal schema carries typeOptions.resultType for all computed types; 98% coverage, 100% of public-ambiguous. Findings in docs. (User reviewed, gave go to proceed.)

title: Internal-API-resolved type disambiguation for codegen
description:
Integrate internal-API discoveries into the code generators, starting with type disambiguation. Computed fields (formula/lookup/rollup/count) have a container type, not a result type; the public meta API often reports formula results as singleLineText/ambiguous (the find_type_ambiguities / analyze_type_consistency population), so typed ORMs (Python/TS/Rust) fall back to generic types on exactly the derived fields users want typed. The internal application/read schema necessarily carries Airtable's resolved result types (the web UI types/sorts/filters these correctly).

Converged design (discussion 2026-06-10):
- SPIKE FIRST: confirm the internal application/read schema carries a resolved resultType for computed fields + its shape; measure coverage vs find_type_ambiguities; capture getUnsavedColumnConfigResultType shape as formula fallback. Go/no-go on schema-first.
- Schema-first resolver: {field_id -> resolved_type} from the internal schema (already fetched via _read_application_data), validator (getUnsavedColumnConfigResultType) as targeted fallback for formulas only.
- PERSISTED TYPE-MAP FILE (CI stays PAT-only): local session-backed command writes resolved types to JSON (mirrors CSV name-locking); CI codegen reads the file, no internal session at build time.
- Integration point: enrich computed fields' result_type BEFORE map_types (src/utils/type_mapper.py); typed generators consume it; graceful fallback to current inference when map absent/field missing.
- Deferred/optional: nightly regression check comparing our inferred types vs Airtable's resolved types.

Other generator-integration ideas parked for later: typed view constants (Contacts.views.active + filter/sort/visible cols), docs by sidebar sections + automation annotations, live filter predicates.
notes: REVERTED 2026-06-11 (commit 2f86813). Negative result: internal application/read resultType is COARSER than public options.result.type (text vs email/url/currency/dateTime); overriding regresses, public-unresolved gap was 14 fields filled 0. Resolver/type-map/integration all removed. Do not re-attempt without a fundamentally different angle.

title: Wire automation refs into find_unused_fields
description:
Consume the automation index in find_unused_fields.
- Add a 4th independent unused-signal: 'not_referenced_by_automations' (fires when no automation references the field).
- When a field IS referenced by automations, surface it as prominent counter-evidence: include automation_references (automation names + where) in that field's output even if other signals fire — so a human sees 'N unused signals BUT used by automation X'. Consider: a field referenced by a deployed automation probably shouldn't be reported as a candidate at all, or should be clearly flagged 'live automation dependency'. Decide during impl.
- Update _UNUSED_FIELD_CAVEATS: remove/soften the 'automations invisible' caveat; note interfaces + external API consumers are still invisible.
- Tests: field used only by an automation must not look dead; field with all 4 signals reported; synthetic automation index via monkeypatch.
notes: DECISION 2026-06-10: option (a) — always report candidates with >= min_signals, but attach a prominent automation_references counter-evidence block when the field IS used by automations. Never suppress. The tool surfaces evidence; the human decides.

title: Tool: audit_shares
description:
Shared function + CLI (tools audit-shares) + MCP (audit_shares) + tests.
- Model: capture sharesById on ViewDefinition (currently extra=ignore drops it) — shape observed: {id: shr..., modelId, createdByUserId, canBeCloned, canBeExported, includeHiddenColumns, includeBlocks, emailDomain, hasPassword, ...}. Also parse base-level sharesById from application/read (same shape, modelId = appXXX).
- Tool: audit_shares(table?) — whole base default. Output: every share with scope (base|view), table/view names where applicable, exposure details, creator, and full URL (https://airtable.com/{shrId}) — unredacted by decision 2026-06-10.
- Summary: counts by scope, exportable count, password-protected count, domain-restricted count.
- Note: whole-base view-share coverage requires the all-views scan (one request per uncached view) — reuse get_all_view_definitions; base-level shares are free.
close_reason: list_interfaces shipped + live-verified (2 interfaces, 1 published, 3 pages).

title: UI-only surfaces: share audit, interfaces, automations
description:
Third wave of internal-API tools — surfaces with NO public API at all (bucket B from the 2026-06-10 discussion). Decisions: full automation config dumps (not just inventory) if the endpoint allows; share URLs included in output unredacted (owner-local tool).

Tools (POC pattern: shared function in src/internal_api/tools.py, thin CLI + MCP adapters, synthetic-fixture tests, structured errors, clean names):
1. audit_shares — every share link in the base with exposure details (exportable, password, domain restriction, hidden columns, creator, full URL). Base-level sharesById from application/read + view-level sharesById that already rides along in view/readData (currently discarded by the model).
2. list_interfaces — pageBundles inventory from application/read (name, icon, pages, publish dates).
3. list_automations — workflow definitions. workflowSectionsById (sections + wfl IDs) already in application/read; reading each workflow's trigger/actions/enabled state needs endpoint discovery first (capture from the Automations tab, same technique as the spike).

Value compounding noted for later (NOT in this epic): automation field references feed a new signal for find_unused_fields and an automations dimension for find_views_using_field.
close_reason: UI-only surfaces epic complete: audit_shares (830 shares, 487 exportable base-wide), list_interfaces, list_automations (full config dumps). 33 MCP tools total.

title: Fetching layer: get_all_view_definitions + column info + cache
description:
Extend src/internal_api/ per the investigation's chosen strategy:
- get_all_view_definitions(table) returning {view_id: ViewDefinition} for every view in a table, using the cheapest verified fetch path (batch table/readData or bounded-concurrency per-view calls)
- Extend TableViews/models with column info (id, name, type) from tableSchemas[].columns — needed to resolve field names and to enumerate fields for visibility analysis
- Row-count capture: keep rowOrder length per view (do NOT serialize rowOrder itself) — expose as ViewDefinition.row_count
- Cache: per-table TTL cache like _read_table_views; whole-base scans must not refetch per tool call
- Handle unreadable personal views gracefully (skip + report, per investigation finding)
close_reason: Fetching layer shipped: concurrent per-view fetch (6 threads), 120s TTL cache, thread-safe transport, row_count + column info on models. Live-verified: 33 views 7.7s cold / 0s warm, 0 errors.

title: Investigate: cheapest batch fetch of all viewDatas per table
description:
Answer before building the view-analysis fetching layer:
1. Can table/{tblId}/readData with includeDataForViewIds=[ALL view ids] + may* flags return all viewDatas in one call, and how does payload scale vs per-view view/{viwId}/readData calls? (Earlier: 1 view included = 11.8MB w/ rows; includeDataForViewIds=[] = 1.3MB with 17 rows and viewDatas=1.)
2. Is there a param combo that returns viewDatas WITHOUT rowOrder/rows? (rowOrder is the only heavy key.)
3. Do non-grid view types (form, kanban, calendar, gallery, levels) return columnOrder/filters in the same shape? Sample one of each from the live base.
4. Are other users' personal views (personalForUserId != null) readable via view/readData, or do they 403? Affects audit_views and find_views_using_field coverage claims.
5. Reliable total-row-count source per table (rowOrder of an unfiltered view? loadedSlices? something in table/readData?).
Deliverable: findings appended to docs/airtable-internal-api.md spike-findings section; chosen fetch strategy recorded in this issue's notes.
notes: DECISION: per-view GET view/{viwId}/readData, bounded concurrency (~6 threads over shared httpx client, which is thread-safe; cookie write-back needs a lock), per-view TTL cache. Batch impossible (includeDataForViewIds max 1 → 422). All view types same shape (form lacks filters/sorts). Personal views of other users readable. Total rows = max(rowOrder len) across views (exact iff an unfiltered view exists). Full findings in docs/airtable-internal-api.md 'Investigation 2026-06-10'.
close_reason: All 5 questions answered against live base; strategy: per-view fetch + concurrency + TTL cache. Findings in docs.

title: View analysis tools: field usage, record counts, hygiene audit, unused fields
description:
Second wave of internal-API read-only tools, composing the POC plumbing (transport + view/readData + application/read) into analysis tools. No new write surface.

Tools (clean names, shared-function + thin CLI/MCP adapter pattern from the POC):
1. find_views_using_field — which views filter/sort/group/color by a field; completes reverse_dependencies (formulas-only today)
2. count_records — per-view row counts from rowOrder lengths (public API can't do this without paging records)
3. audit_views — hygiene: personal views, copy-of names, unfiltered views, stale sorts, creator attribution
4. find_unused_fields — view-aware dead-field analysis: no formula refs (public-API analysis) AND hidden in all views AND in no filter/sort/group (internal API)

Design constraints carried over from POC:
- All logic in src/internal_api/tools.py-style shared functions; CLI (myairtable tools ...) and MCP register thin adapters
- Internal-API code stays in src/internal_api/; public models untouched
- Structured errors, JSON-first CLI output
- Key efficiency problem: these tools need viewDatas for ALL views of a table/base (Contacts alone has 33 views; view/readData is ~470KB each due to rowOrder). Investigation task determines the batch strategy before building.
close_reason: Epic complete: all four view-analysis tools shipped with CLI + MCP adapters, tests, live verification. 30 MCP tools total.

title: Transport + auto-login: src/internal_api/ auth layer
description:
Build src/internal_api/ package per spike findings:
- httpx-based transport with persisted cookie jar + write-back after responses
- Auto-login: on missing/expired session, launch headless Chromium, fill login form from AIRTABLE_EMAIL/AIRTABLE_PASSWORD, wait for app redirect, persist cookies, continue with httpx
- Fail fast: check persisted cookies before any network call so unauthenticated state errors instantly
- Error hierarchy: InternalApiError base; NotAuthenticated (message tells user what's wrong + that public-API tools are unaffected); EndpointShapeChanged (response didn't parse — Airtable likely changed v0.3)
- Required headers per docs §1.5; ID validation regex ^[a-z]{3}[A-Za-z0-9]+$ before building URLs
- Transport (session/headers/retries/errors) cleanly separated from endpoint methods — mutation envelope must be addable later without rewrite
- 'myairtable login' CLI command: headful forced re-auth, debug-only
- Packaging: myairtable[internal] optional extra (playwright/patchright dep); PAT/CI path untouched
notes:
SPIKE OUTCOMES (see docs/airtable-internal-api.md 'Spike findings'):
- Login engine: Playwright FIREFOX headless (NOT Chromium/Patchright — PerimeterX blocks all Chromium automation, even headful real Chrome)
- Login flow quirks: press_sequentially() not fill() (React form); block Transcend consent overlay via ctx.route('*transcend*' -> abort) + remove #transcend-shadow-root; press Enter in password field (submit button stays disabled); two-step email->Continue->password
- httpx transport CONFIRMED (option B): Firefox session cookies + x- headers + Firefox UA + Accept: application/json. No TLS impersonation needed.
- Session lives ~1 YEAR (__Host-airtable-session). Cookie write-back: responses rotate AWSALBTG*/brw/mbpg.
- Dependency: playwright (firefox engine). NOT patchright, NOT msgpack.
- Working reference scripts from spike: /tmp/spike_login_ff.py, /tmp/spike_httpx*.py; live session at ~/.myairtable/spike-profile-ff + spike-state.json
close_reason: Transport + auto-login shipped and verified E2E: cold start auto-logged-in headlessly and served get-view; warm path 1.1s no browser. Session file 0600 at ~/.myairtable/internal-session.json.

title: Spike: verify headless login, httpx transport, and endpoint shapes
description:
Answer in order:
1. Does headless scripted login (email/password from .env) succeed reliably? Try vanilla Playwright first; Patchright if bot-detected; headful as last resort.
2. Does httpx-with-extracted-cookies work for the read endpoints, or does Airtable fingerprint/block plain HTTP? (Required headers from docs §1.5: x-airtable-inter-service-client: webClient, x-requested-with: XMLHttpRequest, x-user-locale, x-time-zone, browser User-Agent. Half-step before full fallback-A: curl_cffi TLS impersonation.)
3. Hit GET /v0.3/getUserProperties, /v0.3/application/{appId}/read, /v0.3/table/{tblId}/readData — compare actual response shapes against docs/airtable-internal-api.md §2 and record divergences in the doc.
4. How long does an HTTP-only session live? Does Airtable rotate/refresh cookies on responses? (Informs cookie write-back design.)

Deliverable: findings written into docs/airtable-internal-api.md (or a spike-findings section), transport decision confirmed (B vs A).
close_reason: All 4 questions answered. Headless login works via Playwright Firefox (Chromium blocked by PerimeterX). httpx transport confirmed. Endpoint shapes verified + divergences documented in docs/airtable-internal-api.md. Session lives ~1yr. Bonus: found undocumented view/{viwId}/readData endpoint — ideal for get_view.

title: Internal API POC: live view definitions via MCP + CLI
description:
POC for Airtable internal v0.3 API integration. Feature: get_view (full live definition: filters, sorts, grouping, column order/visibility, frozen count, color config, row height) + get_view_sections, exposed as both MCP tools and CLI commands.

Converged design decisions (from /discuss 2026-06-10, see docs/airtable-internal-api.md + docs/internal-api-feature-options.md):
- Clean tool names (no internal- prefix/suffix); dev separation lives in module boundaries
- src/internal_api/ fully separate from public-API code: own Pydantic models (do NOT bolt onto src/meta.py View), own error hierarchy (InternalApiError > NotAuthenticated, EndpointShapeChanged)
- Transport: httpx with persisted cookies (option B); Playwright/Patchright only for login; in-page fetch (option A) is fallback if Airtable blocks plain HTTP
- Auth: fully automatic headless login from .env (AIRTABLE_EMAIL/AIRTABLE_PASSWORD, email+password account, no 2FA); cookie write-back to disk to keep logins rare; 'myairtable login' kept only as headful debug command
- POC scope excludes CSRF + secretSocketId (GET-only endpoints need neither); deferred to first write feature
- Transport separated from endpoint methods so mutation envelope (push, formula CLI) lands later without rewrite
- Ships as myairtable[internal] optional extra; PAT/CI path untouched
- Tool logic implemented once as plain functions; MCP and CLI are thin adapters
- CLI output JSON by default for agent-testability
close_reason: POC complete: live view definitions via MCP + CLI, auto-login from .env, all five tasks shipped and E2E-verified.

title: Remove typecast parameter from Swift; match Rust default
description: Swift uniquely exposes typecast while Python/TS/JS/Rust don't. Remove it to match the others — default to false under-the-hood (Rust-style: omit the key from request bodies entirely). The broader effort to add typecast to all targets is tracked at myairtable-hbph.
close_reason: Removed typecast parameter from Swift's public API — matches Rust/Py/TS behavior (Airtable defaults to false). Wire envelopes (AirtableCreateBody/UpdateBody/UpsertBody + DictTable's private structs) no longer include typecast — the JSON body omits the key entirely, matching Rust's static/rust/client.rs approach. All 106 tests still pass (26 integration tests particularly confirm: Airtable accepts single/multi-select option NAMES as strings without typecast, so nothing regressed). Cross-target typecast support tracked at myairtable-hbph.

title: F4.13 — Consolidate table CRUD under overloaded get/create/update/delete (match TS/Py)
description:
Swift currently exposes getOne/createOne/updateOne/deleteOne (+ deleteMany) which doesn't match the TS/Py patterns that use overloaded get/create/update/delete accepting either a single record or a list.

Refactor:
- OrmTable<Model> gains: get(String) -> Model, get([String]) -> [Model], get(AirtableQuery) -> [Model], create(Create) -> Model, create([Create]) -> [Model], update(Model), update([Model]), delete(String), delete([String]), delete(Model), delete([Model]), upsert(Create, matchFieldsToMerge:) -> (Model, Bool)
- Batch variants chunk-by-10 (matches Airtable API limit).
- {Table}Table forwards every overload with @inlinable wrappers.
- Integration tests switch from createOne/getOne/updateOne/deleteOne to create/get/update/delete.
- Pytest generator tests updated to assert new shape.
close_reason: Consolidated table CRUD under overloaded get/create/update/delete matching TS/Py. OrmTable<Model>: get(String)/get([String])/get(AirtableQuery) → Model or [Model]; create(Create)/create([Create]); update(Model)/update([Model]) + updateFields(id, dict); upsert(Create, matchFieldsToMerge:); delete(String)/delete([String])/delete(Model)/delete([Model]). All batch variants chunk by 10 (Airtable API limit). DictTable also refactored — get/create/update/delete with single + batch overloads. {Table}Table struct forwards every overload via @inlinable wrappers (internal OrmTable is @usableFromInline). Parallel dispatch for get([String]) reverted to sequential because Model (@Observable class) isn't Sendable. All 26 integration tests + 39 pytest + 41 static runtime = 106 tests pass.

title: F4.12 — Refactor ORM access: default on table, model-side save/fetch/delete without table param
description:
User feedback after F4 landed. Three changes to align Swift API with Rust/TS/Py:

1. Remove .orm property from {Table}Table — forward ORM methods (getOne,
   getMany, createOne, updateOne, upsertOne, deleteOne, deleteMany) directly
   on the table struct. .dict remains for raw-dict access.

2. Rename `refresh` → `fetch` to match Rust/TS/Py naming.

3. Model-side save/fetch/delete no longer take an OrmTable parameter. Each
   model instance carries a reference to AirtableClient (set by OrmTable after
   decode). model.save() / model.fetch() / model.delete() use the stored ref.

Also requires refactoring OrmTable<Model, Create> → OrmTable<Model> so the
model-side methods can construct the right OrmTable internally without a
Create generic.

Affects:
- static/swift/AirtableModel.swift (protocol + extension methods)
- static/swift/OrmTable.swift (single-generic refactor)
- src/generators/swift.py (write_models: _attachedClient; write_tables: forward methods, drop .orm)
- tests/test_generators.py (content assertions)
- myairtable-tests/swift/Tests/ (integration tests rewrite)
close_reason: Shipped as part of commit a59e316. Superseded by further refactor in F4.13 (myairtable-fvq8 / da56328) which consolidated the fluent model API under overloaded names matching TS/Py.

title: Dirty tracking implementation — explicit snapshot-dict diff
description: Per /tmp/swift-plan-v2.md §5 Feature 4, task 6. Implement dirty tracking as an explicit snapshot-dict diff (NOT @Observable-based). title: F2.10 Test: TestFieldsDualAccess — ID-first, name-fallback semantics
description:
Plan ref: /tmp/swift-plan-v2.md §5 Feature 2, task 10.

Static-runtime unit test covering the Fields struct's dual ID/name lookup semantics from F2.5.

Test cases:
  - get(fieldId) returns stored value directly
  - get(fieldName) resolves via name index and returns the same value
  - ID-first precedence: when a field-name string coincidentally equals another field's ID, the ID match wins
  - get(unknownKey) returns nil
  - set(fieldId, value) then get by name returns the new value
  - set(fieldName, value) then get by ID returns the new value
  - Codable round-trip: encode produces field-ID-keyed JSON, decode rehydrates identical Fields
  - Sendable verification: Fields can cross actor boundaries (compiled-in check)

Requirements:
  - Uses XCTest
  - Constructs Fields with a small synthetic schema (e.g., id 'fld123' ~ name 'Title')

Completion criterion: File tests/swift_static/Tests/MyAirtableStaticTests/TestFieldsDualAccess.swift exists, all cases pass against the F2.5 implementation, collision precedence test proves ID-first resolution.

Files touched:
  - tests/swift_static/Tests/MyAirtableStaticTests/TestFieldsDualAccess.swift (new)

title: F2.6 static/swift/DictTable.swift — Sendable front-end forwarding to actor
description:
Plan ref: /tmp/swift-plan-v2.md §5 Feature 2, task 6.

Implement DictTable — the Sendable struct front-end for raw (non-typed) CRUD operations. It forwards every call to the AirtableClient actor.

description: Net-new from UR. (1) Asymmetric transport-error retry: Rust retries timeouts/connects; Go returns immediately on transport error (client.go:123); TS performMergeUpsert returns immediately (:554). Decide one policy. (2) Retry-After in HTTP-date form silently dropped in Go (Atoi), Rust (parse::<f64>), Swift (Double(raw)); only Java parses RFC-9110 dates -> server backoff signal lost. Add date parsing to all. (3) Rust jitter is weak (subsec_nanos()%1000) and mislabeled 'decorrelated'; move to full jitter. Found in UR.

title: Retry 5xx (incl. 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE) in library-backed targets (TS/JS/Python)
description: The 6 native targets (Rust/Go/Swift/Kotlin/Java/C#) already retry 429+5xx. The 3 library-backed targets only retry 429: airtable.js (base.js:60 retries 429 only; no config to add 5xx) and pyairtable (DEFAULT_RETRIABLE_STATUS_CODES=(429,)). So a 503 surfaces immediately on TS/JS/Python. Fix: TS/JS add a withRetry wrapper around airtable.js calls + the raw-PATCH upsert path (retry 500/502/503/504, exp backoff+jitter, ~5 attempts, 0.5s base, 30s cap; airtable.js error lacks Retry-After header so 503 uses pure backoff). Python: construct pyairtable Api/Table with retry_strategy(status_forcelist=(429,500,502,503,504)). Add deterministic unit tests (mock op throwing 503 then succeeding; assert 4xx not retried; assert pyairtable forcelist includes 5xx).
close_reason: Implemented: TS/JS withRetry wrapper (429/5xx, jittered exp backoff, 5 attempts/0.5s/30s cap) around airtable.js calls + raw-PATCH upsert; Python Api built with retry_strategy(status_forcelist=(429,500,502,503,504)). Deterministic offline unit tests added (retry-then-succeed, no-retry-on-422, give-up-at-max for TS/JS; forcelist assertion for Python) and wired into --crud. py crud 115 passed, ts crud 224 passed.

title: TS/JS: clearing a scalar field via undefined is silently dropped (not cleared server-side)
description: Found by TC7 (myairtable-tywg). In static/typescript/airtable-model.ts + static/javascript/airtable-model.js, writableFields() copied a dirty field's raw undefined value into the update payload; JSON.stringify drops undefined keys, so Airtable never received a clear instruction and single-select/collaborator fields couldn't be cleared (array fields worked because [] survives serialization). Setting null instead is rejected by the .optional() Zod schema. Fix: in writableFields, on update (!_isNew) map an included dirty field's nullish value to JSON null so the cell is cleared. Verified: clearing single-select/collaborator now round-trips to empty across TS+JS; no regression in serializing/crud suites.

title: Runtime: multi-value field coerces to first element instead of joining with ', '
description: Found by TC6 (myairtable-oi85). AirtableRuntime.S() (string coercion) rendered a JSON array (multi-select, multi-value lookup) by taking only the first element (arr[0]) instead of joining all elements with ', ' as Airtable does in string context. E.g. a multiple-select {Option 1, Option 2} referenced in a CONCATENATE rendered 'Option 1' instead of 'Option 1, Option 2'. Affects any user formula referencing a multi-value field in a string context, not just the Primary Complex formula. Fix: S() array case joins elements with ', '. Apply across all 9 runtime targets.

title: Runtime ENCODE_URL_COMPONENT over/under-encodes vs encodeURIComponent (cs/java/kotlin/swift/py)
description:
Found by TC4 (myairtable-qg0r). The transpiled ENCODE_URL_COMPONENT diverged from Airtable (which matches JS encodeURIComponent; unreserved set A-Za-z0-9-_.!~*'()):
- C#/Java/Kotlin: allowed-extra set was the URL-query set '-._~!$&'()*+,;=:@/?' -> wrongly left +,;=:@/?&$ literal.
- Swift: used CharacterSet.urlQueryAllowed (same over-permissive set).
- Python: urllib.parse.quote(safe='') over-encoded !*'().
- Go/TS/JS were already correct.
Fix: cs/java/kotlin allowed-extra -> '-_.!~*'()'; swift -> custom ASCII set; python -> safe="!*'()". Corrected the buggy a&b=c->a&b=c unit assertions in java/kotlin/csharp static suites to a%26b%3Dc, added a+b->a%2Bb. Verified live: 'a.e-i+o' -> 'a.e-i%2Bo' now matches across targets.
close_reason: Fixed ENCODE_URL_COMPONENT in cs/java/kotlin/swift runtime + python emitter to match encodeURIComponent; corrected static unit assertions; verified live across 9 targets

title: TS/JS: surface a typed error hierarchy (parity with C#/Go/Rust/etc.)
description:
Found by TC3 (myairtable-cszk). The TS/JS targets wrap the airtable.js library and flatten all API errors to plain Error(String(error)) in typescript/javascript output static airtable-table — discarding the structured code/statusCode. Gaps vs the other 7 targets:
- No typed error hierarchy (no AirtableError/ApiError/RateLimitedError; underlying airtable.js AirtableError doesn't even extend Error). Consumers can only string-match .message.
- get() short-circuits a missing record id with a client-side Error('Record <id> not found') instead of surfacing the server 404 NOT_FOUND.
- The record-id Zod regex rejects valid-format-but-missing ids before any HTTP call.
- create() silently drops unknown field ids (toWritableRecord filters to known writableFieldIds); no dict/pass-through accessor like the other targets.
- No distinct rate-limited error class.

Scope: rework the TS/JS generator to re-throw a typed error (AirtableError base + ApiError{code,statusCode} + RateLimitedError{retryAfter}) instead of throw new Error(String(error)); stop short-circuiting 404s; relax the id regex; stop silently dropping unknown fields (or add a dict pass-through). This is a BREAKING change to those clients' error contract — deliberate design needed. When done, un-skip typescript/tests/error-paths.test.ts + javascript/tests/error-paths.test.js and rewrite them with real typed assertions mirroring csharp TestErrorPaths.
notes: rxht T4: when this lands, un-skip typescript/tests/error-paths.test.ts + the JS twin (currently describe.skip) so TS/JS regain executing error-classification coverage.
close_reason: Added TS/JS typed error hierarchy (AirtableError base + 7 subclasses: ApiError/RateLimitedError/HttpError/DecodingError/InvalidUrlError/MissingCredentialsError/NetworkError) mirroring C#/Rust/Go/Java/Kotlin/Swift. Two classifiers (classifyAirtableJsError, classifyHttpResponse) parse both envelope shapes; wired into withRetry, performMergeUpsert, get() not-found. Exported via generator barrels (TS + JS). 18 deterministic classifier unit tests pass; error-paths tests un-skipped with typed assertions (also clears rxht T4). tsc clean. Unknown-field allowlist divergence documented. Commits in both repos.

title: List cache stores page-1 payload incl. offset — expired-offset 422s + cross-page staleness (Kotlin + Swift)
description: listRecords caches the raw first page (with its offset token); get(query) then follows offset with UNCACHED live calls. With TTL > Airtable's ~5min offset lifetime, a 'cache hit' on a >100-record query follows a dead offset -> 422 LIST_RECORDS_ITERATOR_NOT_AVAILABLE; also mixes stale page 1 with fresh pages. Cheapest fix: skip cache.set when payload has non-empty offset (multi-page queries become fully live); better: cache the merged list at the table layer. Swift identical (OrmTable.swift:55-70).
close_reason: Both clients now skip caching payloads that carry a non-empty offset continuation token (expires ~5min server-side; a cached one fails the follow-up page fetch). Kotlin: OffsetProbe minimal decode + 4 MockEngine behavioral tests (added ktor-client-mock test dep). Swift: hasContinuationOffset probe + 2 unit tests; full 257-test swift suite green. Live TestCaching 9/9 unaffected. Multi-page queries are now fully live (correct, just uncached); merged-list caching left as a future enhancement.

title: AirtableJson.instance lacks serializersModule — V() silently nulls computed Instant/Duration generics
description: serializer<MaybeSpecialOrError<Instant>>() / VecOrValue<...Instant/Duration> fails (Instant has no resolvable serializer; Duration resolves the BUILT-IN ISO serializer emitting PT5S not seconds); V()'s catch turns it into JsonNull. Impact: toRecord() drops computed date fields; transpiled formulas referencing computed date fields evaluate as BLANK. NOTE narrower than first reported: bare writable Instant/Duration fields are SAFE via the explicit V(Instant?)/V(Duration?) overloads; @file:UseSerializers covers plugin decode. Fix: SerializersModule { contextual(Instant, AirtableInstantSerializer) } (+ Duration handling) on AirtableJson.instance; narrow V()'s catch to SerializationException; add a regression test for V(MaybeSpecialOrError<Instant>).
close_reason: AirtableJson.instance now registers contextual(Instant, AirtableInstantSerializer); V() catch narrowed to SerializationException. Computed date fields (MaybeSpecialOrError<Instant>, VecOrValue nesting) now encode as ISO strings instead of silently degrading to JsonNull in toRecord()/formula evaluation. Duration-in-generics limitation documented in code (built-in serializer shadows contextual; only affects computed duration roll-up formula refs). 3 regression tests; full static suite + live computed/runtime-formula integration green.

title: Rust: VecOrValue<T>::Multiple rejects null items from rollup/lookup arrays
description: Airtable rollup and lookup fields can return arrays containing null items (e.g. [null, 'a', null]). Python models this as 'list[T | None] | T' and zod as 'z.union([T, z.array(T.nullable())])'. Rust's VecOrValue<T>::Multiple(Vec<T>) has no null slot, so serde fails to deserialize these responses.
design:
# Implementation Plan

## Bug
Rollup/lookup fields from Airtable return JSON like `[null, "a", null]` when some linked records are missing the source field. `VecOrValue<T>` in `static/rust/types.rs` is defined as:

```rust
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum VecOrValue<T> {
    Single(T),
    Multiple(Vec<T>),           // ← rejects null items
}
```

Serde fails at the `Vec<T>` level when any item is JSON null, so the entire record deserialize fails.

## Cross-language check
- Python (`type_mapper.py` L302): `union_fmt = "list[{0} | None] | {0}"` → items are nullable
- Zod (L314): `union_fmt = "z.union([{0}, z.array({0}.nullable())])"` → items are nullable
- TypeScript (L308): `union_fmt = "{0} | {0}[]"` → non-nullable (likely also a latent bug, but out of scope here)
- Rust (L322): `union_fmt = "VecOrValue<{0}>"` → Multiple variant's items are non-nullable

## Fix
Change the `Multiple` variant in `static/rust/types.rs` from `Vec<T>` to `Vec<Option<T>>`:

```rust
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum VecOrValue<T> {
    Single(T),
    Multiple(Vec<Option<T>>),
}
```

Variant order (Single before Multiple) still correct — a bare JSON null at the top level would not match either variant, which is desirable (the whole field is wrapped in `Option<...>` at the struct level, so field-level null is already handled by the outer Option).

## Why not change the format string
Considered setting `union_fmt = "VecOrValue<Option<{0}>>"`. Rejected: that makes `Single` also `Option<T>`, which is wrong — when Airtable returns a single value it is never null at that position (null comes as the field missing entirely, handled by the outer `Option` on the field). Only the list-case items need nullability.

## Interaction with myairtable-wrr (special types)
When myairtable-wrr lands with `computed_union_fmt = "VecOrValue<MaybeSpecialOrError<{0}>>"`, the fixed `Multiple(Vec<Option<MaybeSpecialOrError<T>>>)` correctly accepts `[null, 42, {"error":"#ERROR!"}, {"specialValue":"NaN"}]`. No additional changes needed once both land. These two issues can be implemented independently.

## Changes

### 1. `static/rust/types.rs`
- `Multiple(Vec<T>)` → `Multiple(Vec<Option<T>>)`
- Update doc comment to note that list items are nullable to reflect Airtable rollup/lookup behavior

### 2. `tests/test_rust_static.rs`
Update existing test `vec_or_value_deserializes_multiple` to match new shape. Add:
- `[null, "a", null]` → `Multiple` with mixed `Some`/`None`
- `[null]` → `Multiple` with one `None`
- `[]` → `Multiple` empty
- Single-value case unchanged (`"hello"` still `Single`)
- Serialize round-trip: `Multiple(vec![Some("a".into()), None])` → `["a", null]`

### 3. No changes needed in:
- `src/utils/type_mapper.py` — format string stays the same; the enum definition change carries the fix through
- `src/generators/rust.py` — `VecOrValue` is already in `_STATIC_TYPES`
- Generated model files — existing `Option<VecOrValue<T>>` fields automatically get the new semantics

## Validation
- `cargo test --test test_rust_static` — new null-in-list tests pass
- Regenerate a base with rollup fields and deserialize a real Airtable response — no panic
- `pytest` — confirm no regressions in Python generator tests (should be unaffected)

## Blast radius
Low. Only consumer of `VecOrValue::Multiple` currently is generated ORM code that reads the field via the enum pattern match. Any downstream code pattern-matching on `Multiple(vec)` and indexing directly into `T` will now need to handle `Option<T>`. Since the Rust SDK is new and has no known external consumers yet, this cost is acceptable — and the alternative (silently dropping records with null rollup items) is worse.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rust: handle formula special values (errors, specialNumbers)
description: The Rust implementation needs to account for Airtable special types returned by formula/computed fields: error objects like {error: '#ERROR!'} and special numbers like {specialValue: 'NaN'}. Mirror the zod approach in special-types.ts — add SpecialNumber, ErrorValue, and generic wrapper enums to static/rust/types.rs, then update the type mapper to wrap computed field types accordingly (numeric computed → MaybeSpecial<T>, other computed → MaybeError<T>; lookup/rollup uses VecOrValue of these).
design:
# Implementation Plan

## Context
- TS/zod handles Airtable's special values for computed fields via `static/typescript/special-types.ts`:
  - `SpecialNumberSchema = z.object({ specialValue: z.string() })` — e.g. `{specialValue: "NaN"}` / `"Infinity"`
  - `ErrorValueSchema = z.object({ error: z.string() })` — e.g. `{error: "#ERROR!"}`
- zod wraps computed field types (see `src/utils/type_mapper.py::map_zod_type`):
  - Numeric computed (INTEGER/FLOAT/DURATION): `z.union([T, SpecialNumberSchema, ErrorValueSchema])`
  - Non-numeric computed: `z.union([T, ErrorValueSchema])`
  - Lookup/rollup computed: via `computed_union_fmt`, wraps both single and array cases with Special+Error
- Python side sanitizes at runtime (`static/python/table_helpers.py::sanitize_record_dict` coerces special values to `None`)
- Rust currently has `computed_union_fmt=""` in `LANGUAGE_CONFIGS["rust"]` — no special-value handling at all; serde deserialization would fail when Airtable returns these objects into strongly-typed fields

## Goal
Mirror the zod type-level approach for Rust using `#[serde(untagged)]` enums. Match zod's wrapping rules exactly.

## Changes

### 1. `static/rust/types.rs` — add types

```rust
/// An Airtable special number value (NaN, Infinity).
/// JSON shape: `{"specialValue": "NaN"}`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SpecialNumber {
    #[serde(rename = "specialValue")]
    pub special_value: String,
}

/// An Airtable error value from a failed formula.
/// JSON shape: `{"error": "#ERROR!"}`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ErrorValue {
    pub error: String,
}

/// Value, special number, or error. For numeric computed fields.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum MaybeSpecialOrError<T> {
    Value(T),
    Special(SpecialNumber),
    Error(ErrorValue),
}

/// Value or error. For non-numeric computed fields.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum MaybeError<T> {
    Value(T),
    Error(ErrorValue),
}
```

Variant-order matters for `#[serde(untagged)]` — put `Value` first so primitives match before the object-shaped fallbacks.

### 2. `src/utils/type_mapper.py` — mapping logic

a. **LanguageConfig** for rust: set
   `computed_union_fmt = "VecOrValue<MaybeSpecialOrError<{0}>>"` — mirrors zod's unconditional inclusion of both Special + Error for the lookup/rollup case.

b. Add a helper `apply_rust_computed_wrapping(rust_type, resolved, field) -> str` that wraps non-lookup computed fields:
   - Numeric (INTEGER/FLOAT/DURATION) → `MaybeSpecialOrError<T>`
   - Other → `MaybeError<T>`
   - Skip when field involves lookup or rollup (already handled by `computed_union_fmt` in `render_type`)
   - Skip when not computed

c. Call the helper in three places so all code paths stay consistent:
   - `map_types()` after `render_type(field, "rust", ...)`
   - `map_rust_type()` after `render_type(...)`
   - `apply_disambiguated_type()` after `render_type(field, "rust", is_list=...)`

### 3. `src/generators/rust.py` — imports

Extend `_STATIC_TYPES` to include the new names so they are pulled into the `use crate::types::{...}` line of each model file:
- `SpecialNumber`, `ErrorValue`, `MaybeSpecialOrError`, `MaybeError`

(`_collect_static_imports()` already does a substring match on each field's rust_type string, which will pick these up.)

### 4. `tests/test_rust_static.rs` — serde round-trip tests

- `SpecialNumber` deserializes `{"specialValue":"NaN"}` and `"Infinity"`
- `ErrorValue` deserializes `{"error":"#ERROR!"}`
- `MaybeSpecialOrError<f64>` matches each variant: plain number, special-object, error-object
- `MaybeError<String>` matches plain string and error-object
- `VecOrValue<MaybeSpecialOrError<i64>>` matches a mixed array `[1, {"specialValue":"NaN"}, {"error":"#ERROR!"}]`
- Variant-order smoke test: `MaybeSpecialOrError::<f64>` from `42.0` parses as `Value`, not misinterpreted

### 5. Validation
- `cargo check` / `cargo test --test test_rust_static` pass
- Regenerate a sample base and `cargo check` the generated crate to confirm imports resolve and field types compile
- `pytest` on existing Python generator tests to confirm no regressions in non-rust code paths

## Out of scope
- Helper methods on the enums (e.g. `.value()`, `.is_error()`) — can be added later if needed
- Serialization-side handling (these are read-only by construction — computed fields are never written back)
- Runtime sanitization à la Python (different philosophy; user explicitly pointed at the zod/TS approach)
close_reason: Implemented per plan: added SpecialNumber/ErrorValue/MaybeSpecialOrError/MaybeError to static/rust/types.rs; set computed_union_fmt + apply_rust_computed_wrapping helper in type_mapper.py; helper also handles the disambiguated Vec<T> case with Vec<Option<MaybeSpecialOrError<T>>> wrapping (expanded beyond the original plan to keep nullability + computed-union behavior on disambiguated lookup/rollup fields). Extended _STATIC_TYPES. Added 7 serde round-trip tests; all 21 rust_static tests pass, 566 python tests pass.

title: Rust generator ignores custom model names from tables.csv
description:
The Rust generator hardcodes model/create struct names as `{pascal}Model` / `Create{pascal}Model` instead of routing through `table.name_model()` like PY/TS/JS do. As a result, the `Model Name (snake_case)` column in `tables.csv` is ignored by the Rust output.

Affected sites in `src/generators/rust.py`:
- L498-499: `model_name` / `create_name` in `write_models`
- L731: import line in `airtable.rs` generation
- L738-739: per-table wrapper `model` / `create` names
- L945-946: re-export in `lib.rs` generation

Fix: replace `f"{table.name_pascal()}Model"` with `table.name_model()` and `f"Create{table.name_pascal()}Model"` with `f"Create{table.name_model()}"`. Default behavior is preserved (`name_model()` falls back to `pascal + 'Model'`), and custom names from the CSV start flowing through.

See `src/meta.py:250-267` for `name_model()` and `src/generators/csv.py` for the `MODEL_NAME` column.
close_reason: Replaced hardcoded {pascal}Model pattern with table.name_model() at all 4 sites in src/generators/rust.py (write_models + write_lib: model struct decl, per-table use_decl, per-table wrapper, top-level re-export). Custom model names from tables.csv now flow through; default unchanged since name_model() falls back to pascal+'Model'. 566 python tests pass.

title: Rust/TS/JS/Python clients lack a generated merge-field upsert (parity gap vs cs/go/java/kotlin/swift)
description:
Found by TC10 (myairtable-1ehw). C#/Go/Java/Kotlin/Swift expose a first-class merge-field upsert: upsert(model, fieldsToMergeOn) sending Airtable performUpsert.fieldsToMergeOn and returning UpsertResult{model, wasCreated}. Gaps:
- Rust: at.primary.upsert(&mut model) is id-based create/update only (no fieldsToMergeOn, no was_created, no performUpsert). client.rs update_records hardcodes the body.
- TS/JS: upsert(records) is client-side id-based (get-then-create/update); no mergeOn param, no performUpsert, no wasCreated.
- Python: NO generated upsert wrapper at any layer; TC10 reached pyairtable Table.batch_upsert via the ._table escape hatch.
Add a generated merge-field upsert to these 4 targets mirroring C#'s UpsertResult. Until then TC10 covers only cs/go/java/kotlin/swift (+ python via the pyairtable escape hatch).
close_reason: Merge-field upsert (server-side performUpsert) implemented + tested in all 4 languages: Python (extend upsert), Rust (upsert + upsert_many + client.upsert_records), TS/JS (UpsertOptions.fieldsToMergeOn via raw PATCH). TC10 upsert-depth tests pass live (multi-field merge key, multiple-match 422, batch).

title: Rust client has no 429/5xx retry loop (parity gap vs cs/java/kotlin/swift/go)
description: Noted during TC8 (myairtable-i9jf). The hand-rolled clients in C#/Java/Kotlin/Swift (retry-with-jitter, see TestClientHardening) and Go (review_fixes_test, retry on 5xx) retry transient 429/5xx with backoff. The Rust client (static/rust/client.rs) has NO retry loop — a non-success response is returned immediately (a 429 becomes AirtableError::RateLimited after myairtable-cszk). Decide whether the Rust client should gain a retry-with-backoff loop for parity (honoring Retry-After), and add a flaky-transport unit test like the other targets. Python/TS/JS delegate retry to pyairtable/airtable.js.
close_reason: Added 429/5xx + connect/timeout retry to the Rust client (send_with_retry: clone-per-attempt, honor Retry-After, jittered exponential backoff capped 30s, max 5 retries). retry_delay_secs is a pub assoc fn with a unit test; loop validated by TC9 under load. A mock-transport end-to-end test would need a base-URL seam (not added).

title: Runtime transpiler: transcendental precision + empty-input error-semantics differ from Airtable
description:
Found by TC4 (myairtable-qg0r). Two inherent runtime-formula fidelity gaps vs Airtable (V8), documented in csharp TestRuntimeFormulaVariety:
1. Transcendental precision: LOG/SQRT/EXP/POWER results differ by ~1 ULP between each target's math lib and Airtable for irrational results (e.g. LOG(5) -> API ...187 vs C# ...189). Exact string compare is therefore non-portable; TC4 uses clean inputs (powers of 10 / perfect squares). A robust fix would need per-function float-formatting parity or tolerant numeric comparison.
2. Empty-input error semantics: for an all-blank text record, Airtable returns blank for the whole Text formula (e.g. REPLACE past end-of-string errors and poisons the concatenation), while the transpiled runtime is lenient and returns 'LEN: 0; MID: ; ...'. Decide whether the transpiler should replicate Airtable's error propagation on edge inputs.
notes: TC6 adds a 3rd documented runtime limitation: formulas that REFERENCE computed/formula fields (created/modified time+by, auto-number, other formula fields, links/lookups/rollups) can't be reproduced offline — the runtime evaluates from input fields and decodes computed fields as special/wrapped/display-less values. Primary Formula(Complex) computed-field lines and Formula(Nested) are therefore not offline-matchable; only deterministic input-field lines are asserted.
close_reason: Accept + document (decided 2026-06-26). The three offline-eval fidelity gaps are inherent: (1) transcendental ~1 ULP differences are libm divergence vs V8 — unfixable without reimplementing math; (2) empty-input error propagation is a high-effort/fragile model for a degenerate edge case; (3) computed-field references have no data offline (impossible). Already documented in csharp TestRuntimeFormulaVariety + TC4/TC6 notes; tests use clean inputs / deterministic lines. No code change.

title: Add typecast option to create/update/upsert across all languages
description:
Airtable's API supports a `typecast` flag on POST /records and PATCH /records that:
- allows sending option NAMES as strings for single-select / multi-select (works even without typecast, actually — more on this below)
- auto-resolves collaborator fields by email or name
- auto-resolves linked-record fields by primary-key value
- auto-creates new select options when the base allows it

Currently exposed in:
- **Swift**: removed in myairtable-XXXX (this issue's immediate predecessor) to match the other targets. Defaults to false under the hood (envelope field omitted entirely, Rust-style).
- **Rust**: not exposed; omitted from request body.
- **Python**: not exposed in our static orm_table/dict_table. pyAirtable supports it as `typecast: bool = False`.
- **TypeScript / JavaScript**: not exposed in our static tables. airtable.js supports it via `OptionalParameters.typecast`.

Task: add `typecast: Bool = false` to every target's create / update / upsert surface:
1. Python: thread through orm_table + dict_table → pyAirtable.
2. TypeScript + JavaScript: thread through airtable-table → airtable.js Options.
3. Rust: thread through OrmTable + StructTable; include the key in the request body only when true.
4. Swift: re-add typecast param on OrmTable/DictTable/{Table}Table/save(); emit through AirtableCreateBody/UpdateBody/UpsertBody.

Also: consider documenting the safety semantics (auto-option-creation requires the base's schema setting to be enabled) in each target's doc comments.

Integration tests: add a new suite that exercises typecast=true behavior — e.g., create a record passing an auto-creatable new select option, verify the option was created.

Non-goals: dict access. pyAirtable and airtable.js already surface typecast on the raw path; we only need to plumb it through our ORM wrappers.

design:
# Plan: Linked Record Objects (myairtable-ca8)

## Context

Currently Rust link fields are `Option<Vec<RecordId>>` — raw arrays of ID strings. TypeScript wraps these in `LinkedRecord<T>` (single) and `LinkedRecords<T>` (multiple) objects that can lazily fetch the linked model. We need typed linked record wrappers for the Rust ORM.

## Design

### New static runtime types: `static/rust/linked_record.rs`

```rust
/// A single linked record (wraps one RecordId).
pub struct LinkedRecord<T: OrmModel> {
    id: Option<RecordId>,
    cached: Option<T>,
    client: Option<Arc<AirtableClient>>,
    table_id: Option<&'static str>,
}

/// Multiple linked records (wraps Vec<RecordId>).
pub struct LinkedRecords<T: OrmModel> {
    ids: Vec<RecordId>,
    cached: Option<Vec<T>>,
    client: Option<Arc<AirtableClient>>,
    table_id: Option<&'static str>,
}
```

**Methods on LinkedRecord<T>:**
- `id() -> Option<&str>` — get the linked record ID
- `set(&mut self, id: RecordId)` — set the linked ID
- `clear(&mut self)` — remove the link
- `async get(&mut self) -> Result<Option<&T>>` — fetch and cache the linked model
- `async fetch(&mut self) -> Result<Option<T>>` — fetch without caching

**Methods on LinkedRecords<T>:**
- `ids() -> &[RecordId]` — get all linked IDs
- `set(&mut self, ids: Vec<RecordId>)` — replace all links
- `add(&mut self, id: RecordId)` — append a link
- `clear(&mut self)` — remove all links
- `len() -> usize`
- `is_empty() -> bool`
- `async get(&mut self) -> Result<&[T]>` — fetch and cache all linked models
- `async fetch(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<T>>` — fetch without caching

### Serialization

Both types need custom Serialize/Deserialize:
- **Serialize**: `LinkedRecord<T>` → serializes as single-element array `[id]` (Airtable API format). `LinkedRecords<T>` → serializes as `[id1, id2, ...]`
- **Deserialize**: From `[id]` or `[id1, id2, ...]` arrays (what the API returns)

### Generated model changes

Currently:
```rust
pub link_single: Option<Vec<RecordId>>,
pub link_multiple: Option<Vec<RecordId>>,
```

After:
```rust
pub link_single: Option<LinkedRecord<SecondaryModel>>,
pub link_multiple: Option<LinkedRecords<SecondaryModel>>,
```

This requires:
1. The type mapper to return `LinkedRecord<SecondaryModel>` for single-link fields and `LinkedRecords<SecondaryModel>` for multi-link fields
2. The generator to import the linked model type
3. The linked record wrappers to receive the client when the parent model gets `set_client()`

### Challenge: Client propagation

When OrmTable calls `record_to_model()`, it sets the client on the model. But the linked record wrappers inside the model also need the client to fetch. Options:

1. **Lazy**: Wrappers get the client when `.get()` is called, passed as a parameter
2. **Eager**: Override `set_client()` on generated models to propagate to linked fields
3. **Shared**: Wrappers access client from the parent model's `_meta`

Option 1 is simplest — `.get()` takes a client reference:
```rust
let secondary = model.link_single.as_mut().unwrap().get(&client).await?;
```

But this is less ergonomic than TypeScript where you just do `await model.linkSingle.get()`.

Option 3 is best for ergonomics but requires the wrapper to hold `Arc<AirtableClient>`. The generator can propagate in `set_client()` / `apply_record()`.

### Type mapper changes

Need a new Rust-specific rendering for link fields. Currently both `RECORD_ID` and `LIST_OF_RECORD_IDS` map to `Vec<RecordId>`. Need:
- `RECORD_ID` (single link) → `LinkedRecord<{LinkedModel}Model>`
- `LIST_OF_RECORD_IDS` (multi link) → `LinkedRecords<{LinkedModel}Model>`
- For non-link fields that happen to be RECORD_ID, keep as `Vec<RecordId>`

This is tricky because the type mapper doesn't have per-field context about which model to link to. The linked table info is on `field.options.linked_table_id`. The generator needs to handle link fields specially rather than relying purely on the type mapper.

### Implementation steps

1. **Create `static/rust/linked_record.rs`** with `LinkedRecord<T>` and `LinkedRecords<T>`, custom serde, and fetch methods
2. **Update `static/rust/lib.rs`** to include the module
3. **Update generator `write_models()`** to:
   - Detect `multipleRecordLinks` fields
   - Look up `field.linked_table()` to get the linked table name
   - Use `LinkedRecord<{Table}Model>` or `LinkedRecords<{Table}Model>` as the field type
   - Import linked model types
   - Generate `set_client` propagation for linked fields
4. **Update `apply_record()` / `set_client()`** to propagate client to linked record wrappers
5. **Add tests**

### Scope limitation

For MVP, skip:
- Proxy-based chaining (TypeScript's `await primary.linkSingle.linkToTertiary`)
- Thenable syntax (not possible in Rust without ugly hacks)

Focus on:
- Typed wrappers with `.id()` / `.ids()` access
- `.get()` for lazy fetching
- `.set()` / `.add()` for mutation
- Proper serde for API round-trip

## Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `static/rust/linked_record.rs` | **New** — LinkedRecord<T> and LinkedRecords<T> |
| `static/rust/lib.rs` | Add module |
| `src/generators/rust.py` | Update `write_models()` for linked record types |
| `src/utils/type_mapper.py` | May need Rust-specific link field handling |
| `myairtable-tests/rust/tests/test_orm_crud_via_model.rs` | Linked record tests |

## Verification

1. `cd myairtable && cargo check && cargo test`
2. `cd myairtable-tests && ./build.sh && ./test.sh rs`
close_reason: Closing — wrapper types (LinkedRecord<T>/LinkedRecords<T>) are not ergonomic in Rust due to ownership, client propagation, and serde complexity. Plain Vec<RecordId> with explicit two-step fetching is the idiomatic Rust approach.

design:
# Plan: ORM Instance Methods (save/delete/fetch/dirty tracking)

## Context

The current ORM models are passive data structs. They need to become active objects like TypeScript's AirtableModel, with instance methods that call the API directly.

## Required Capabilities (from TypeScript model-crud-via-model tests)

1. **Constructor**: `PrimaryModel { primary_key: Some("Hello"), ..Default::default() }` (already works)
2. **`save()`**: Creates if no `id`, updates if `id` exists. Only sends dirty/new fields.
3. **`fetch()`**: Fetches record data from API by `id`, populates all fields.
4. **`delete()`**: Deletes the record via API.
5. **`from_id(id)`**: Creates model with just an ID (for later fetch).
6. **Dirty tracking**: Tracks which fields changed since last fetch/save. save() only sends dirty fields on update.
7. **Client reference**: Model holds Arc<AirtableClient> + table_id so it can make API calls.

## Design Challenges

### Client on the model
Models need a client to call save/fetch/delete. Options:
- Store `Arc<AirtableClient>` on each model instance
- Use a thread-local or global client
- Pass client to save/fetch/delete as a parameter

Storing on the model matches TS/Python. But it means the model struct gets heavier and can't be Default without a client. Alternative: models returned from OrmTable already have the client set. Manually created models need `with_client()` or are constructed via a factory.

### Dirty tracking in Rust
TypeScript uses a `Set<string>` of dirty field names. In Rust, we could:
- Use a `HashSet<&'static str>` of field IDs
- Use a bitfield (one bit per field, generated)
- Track at the field level with wrapper types

HashSet is simplest and matches TS. The model stores `_dirty: HashSet<String>` and `_is_new: bool`.

### Serialization for save()
On create (new): serialize all non-None fields.
On update (existing): serialize only dirty fields. This needs a custom serializer or a runtime filter. Simplest: build a `serde_json::Value` map manually from dirty fields only.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1: Add model metadata to generated models
Each model gets additional fields (skip_serializing):
- `_client: Option<Arc<AirtableClient>>`
- `_table_id: Option<&'static str>`
- `_is_new: bool`
- `_dirty: HashSet<String>`

### Step 2: Add instance methods to generated models
- `with_client(client, table_id) -> Self` — attaches client
- `from_id(client, table_id, id) -> Self` — creates from ID
- `async save(&mut self) -> Result<()>` — create or update
- `async fetch(&mut self) -> Result<()>` — populate from API
- `async delete(&self) -> Result<()>` — delete record
- `is_new() -> bool`
- `has_changes() -> bool`

### Step 3: Update OrmTable to attach client to returned models
OrmTable.get_one/create_one/etc. should call `model.with_client()` before returning.

### Step 4: Tests
Match TypeScript model-crud-via-model.test.ts:
- Primary key only: new() -> save() -> fromId() -> fetch() -> mutate -> save() -> delete()
- All simple properties
- Linked records
- Attachments
- Users
- Computed fields
- Invalid IDs

## Key Files
- `src/generators/rust.py` — generate instance methods on model structs
- `static/rust/orm_table.rs` — attach client to returned models
- `static/rust/types.rs` — may need OrmModel trait updates
- New test file: `rust/tests/test_orm_crud_via_model.rs`
close_reason: ORM instance methods: save() (create/update with dirty tracking), fetch(), delete(), from_id(), mark_dirty(), has_changes(). 5 model-via-model tests.

# Plan: Rust ORM Models + OrmTable

## Context

Adding typed ORM layer alongside the existing dict layer. Both are fields on `Airtable`:

```rust
airtable.primary.get_one(&id, true).await?;       // Dict -> Record (StructTable, unchanged)
airtable.primary_orm.get_one(&id).await?;          // ORM -> ModelRecord<PrimaryModel>
```

Both use `use_field_ids: true` under the hood. ORM models use `#[serde(rename = "fldXXX")]` for field ID → property name mapping. Dict layer completely untouched.

## New static runtime

### `types.rs` — add two generic types

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ModelRecord<T> {
    pub id: RecordId,
    pub fields: T,
    #[serde(rename = "createdTime")]
    pub created_time: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct ModelPaginatedResponse<T> {
    pub records: Vec<ModelRecord<T>>,
    pub offset: Option<String>,
}
```

### `client.rs` — add generic typed methods

New methods alongside existing ones (existing untouched):

- `get_record_typed<T: DeserializeOwned>(table_id, record_id) -> Result<ModelRecord<T>>`
- `list_records_typed<T: DeserializeOwned>(table_id, params) -> Result<ModelPaginatedResponse<T>>`
- `create_record_typed<T: DeserializeOwned, U: Serialize>(table_id, fields) -> Result<ModelRecord<T>>`
- `update_record_typed<T: DeserializeOwned, U: Serialize>(table_id, record_id, fields) -> Result<ModelRecord<T>>`

All hardcode `returnFieldsByFieldId: true`. Delete methods reuse existing (no return type difference).

### `orm_table.rs` — new static file

```rust
pub struct OrmTable<T, C> {
    client: Arc<AirtableClient>,
    table_id: &'static str,
    table_name: &'static str,
    _phantom: PhantomData<(T, C)>,
}
```

Methods: `get_one`, `get_many`, `create_one`, `create_many`, `update_one`, `update_many`, `delete_one`, `delete_many`. Delegates to typed client methods.

### `lib.rs` — add orm_table module

## Generated code

### `write_models()` — new function

Generates `dynamic/models/{table}.rs`:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
```

design:
# Plan: Runtime Formula Evaluation (myairtable-2uj)

## Context

Python and TypeScript can evaluate Airtable formula fields locally on model instances, without hitting the API. This is done by transpiling Airtable formulas to native code at code-generation time, then executing them on-demand via an `evaluate_formulas_at_runtime` flag.

## Scope Assessment

This is a **very large** feature with three major components:

### 1. Rust Runtime Library (~500 lines)
A `static/rust/airtable_runtime.rs` implementing 44+ Airtable functions:
- Math: SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, CEILING, FLOOR, LOG, EVEN, ODD, MIN, MAX, POWER, MOD, VALUE
- String: LEFT, RIGHT, MID, FIND, SEARCH, SUBSTITUTE, REPLACE, LOWER, UPPER, TRIM, CONCATENATE, REPT, LEN, T
- Date: DATEADD, DATETIME_DIFF, DATETIME_FORMAT, WEEKDAY, WEEKNUM, TODAY, NOW, IS_SAME, IS_BEFORE, IS_AFTER, TONOW, FROMNOW, WORKDAY, WORKDAY_DIFF
- Array: ARRAYJOIN, ARRAYUNIQUE, ARRAYCOMPACT, ARRAYFLATTEN
- Logic: IF, IFS, SWITCH, AND, OR, NOT, TRUE, FALSE, BLANK
- Special: ERROR, ISERROR, RECORD_ID

### 2. Transpiler Extension (~200 lines)
Add a `"rust"` target to the existing `CodeEmitter` in `src/formulas/formula_transpiler.py`:
- Map Airtable AST nodes to Rust expressions
- Handle field references as `self.{field_name}`
- Handle type coercion (Rust is strictly typed)
- Handle linked record dereferencing
- Output valid Rust code strings

### 3. Generator Integration (~50 lines)
In `src/generators/rust.py`, for each formula field on a model:
- Transpile the formula to Rust
- Generate a computed method on the model that evaluates the formula
- Add an `evaluate_formulas_at_runtime` flag

## Challenges

**Rust-specific issues:**
- Strict typing: Airtable formulas are dynamically typed. Rust needs explicit type handling. The runtime would likely operate on `serde_json::Value` internally and coerce as needed.
- No `eval()`: Unlike Python/TypeScript, Rust can't evaluate strings at runtime. The transpiled code must be valid Rust **at compile time**, embedded in the generated model.
- Ownership: Formula expressions reference other fields on `self`, which complicates mutable access.
- Error handling: Every operation could fail; need graceful handling matching Airtable's semantics (return BLANK on error).

**Transpiler issues:**
- The existing transpiler (873 lines) targets Python/TypeScript/JavaScript. Adding Rust requires understanding Rust's syntax for closures, Option handling, type casting, etc.
- Type inference in Rust is different — the transpiler would need to emit explicit conversions.

## Recommendation

This is **P4 for a reason**. It's 500+ lines of new Rust code, 200+ lines of transpiler changes, and significant testing surface. The Rust SDK is already functional without it — formula fields return their API values, which is correct for most use cases.

**If proceeding**, I'd suggest a phased approach:
1. **Phase 1**: Runtime library with core functions (math, string, logic)
2. **Phase 2**: Transpiler Rust target
3. **Phase 3**: Generator integration + tests

**Estimated effort**: 2-3 full sessions.

## Files (if implemented)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `static/rust/airtable_runtime.rs` | **New** — 500+ lines, all Airtable functions |
| `src/formulas/formula_transpiler.py` | Add Rust code emitter target |
| `src/generators/rust.py` | Transpile formulas, add computed methods to models |
| `myairtable-tests/rust/tests/test_runtime_formulas.rs` | **New** — matching Python/TypeScript test patterns |

## Verification

1. Unit tests for each runtime function
2. Integration tests comparing API formula values vs runtime-computed values
3. `cd myairtable-tests && ./build.sh && ./test.sh rs`
close_reason: All subtasks complete: math/logic (8ho), strings (rcz), date/time (7fw), array/special (g89). 157 runtime tests passing.
